name: ip
description: The modern iproute2 tool for interfaces, addresses, routes, and more — the official replacement for ifconfig, route, and arp.

flags.description: -link: show interface state and hardware info; ip link set dev eth0 up brings an interface up.
-route: show kernel routing table; ip route add adds routes.
Colorized output (also always the default on newer iproute2).

examples.output:
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500
    inet 192.168.1.20/24 brd 192.168.1.255 scope global eth0
    inet6 fe80::5054:ff:fe12:3456/64 scope link
examples.explanation: Shows interfaces with their IPv4/IPv6 addresses. This machine has 192.168.1.20/24 on eth0.

examples.output:
lo     UNKNOWN  127.0.0.1/8
eth0   UP       192.168.1.20/24
wlan0  DOWN
examples.explanation: Brief mode: one line per interface — the fastest "what is my IP" check.

examples.output:
default via 192.168.1.1 dev eth0 proto dhcp
192.168.1.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link
examples.explanation: The routing table: default gateway is 192.168.1.1 on eth0. No gateway here means no internet.

examples.command: sudo ip addr add 192.168.1.50/24 dev eth0
examples.explanation: Adds a temporary IP address — lost at reboot; persist it in NetworkManager or netplan/systemd-networkd config.

examples.command: sudo ip link set dev eth0 up
examples.explanation: Brings an interface up (down disables it).

about: ip replaces the deprecated net-tools suite (ifconfig, route, arp, netstat) with a coherent object model. Net-tools is unmaintained and misses features such as policy routing and multiple addresses per interface. Distribution netconfig tools (NetworkManager, systemd-networkd, netplan) persist what ip changes temporarily.
useCases: Check your IP addresses and routes.
mistakes: Expecting ip changes to survive reboots — they are runtime-only.
Confusing ip a (addresses) with ip l (link state): an interface can be UP with no address.
warnings: ip link set down on a remote server can cut your SSH access instantly if you are on that interface.
